proofs.proof_tex:
Fix one member of \(\mathfrak M\).  All probabilities below are conditional on its deterministic complete baseline array.  Write \(P_{0,T}\) for the uniform law on \(\Omega_T\), put \(k=|T|\), and write
\[
X_{T,\beta}=\sqrt{k}\{\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(0)-\boldsymbol\tau_T\}.
\]
The bounded-baseline condition and the positive lower bound on the empirical baseline Gram matrix imply the negligible-maximum-influence condition in every nonzero covariate direction: the numerator is bounded while the corresponding total quadratic variation is of order \(k\).  Conditional boundedness of the potential outcomes gives the same condition for every nondegenerate linear combination of the factorial-outcome coordinates.  The random-partition central limit theorem in \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}population\text{-}random\text{-}partition\text{-}clt}\), applied by Cram\'{e}r--Wold, therefore gives the joint limit
\[
(X_{T,\beta},Z_T)\ 
ightsquigarrow\ (U_\beta,Z),
\qquad Z\sim N(0,I_{Fp}),
\tag{1}
\]
after the nonsingular covariance standardization of the imbalance.  Here \(Z_T\) denotes that standardized imbalance.  The limiting covariance is obtained from the empirical conditional first and second moments.  Those moments and their first three \(\rho\)-derivatives are uniformly bounded and continuous on the compact baseline domain by \(\mathrm{ass{:}arraywise\text{-}moment\text{-}regularity}\); weak convergence of the empirical baseline measure and compactness of \(\mathcal K\) therefore make (1) uniform in \(\beta\).  The same calculation applies to every random complement whose size tends to infinity: simple-random-sampling variance gives, for each bounded continuous empirical-moment coordinate \(h\),
\[
E_{S_m}\left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_m^c}h(x_{in})
-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n h(x_{in})\right|^2
\leq \frac{C_h}{N},
\tag{2}
\]
uniformly when \(N/n\) is bounded away from zero, and the same conclusion follows from \(m/n\to0\) when the complement is asymptotically full.  Finite nets in the compact parameter set and the uniform derivative bounds upgrade (2) to uniformity in \(\beta\).  Thus the full array and every such random complement have the same joint Gaussian limit.  This extends the already established oracle-map convergence in \(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\) to the first-order joint covariance needed here.

Let \(H_T=G_T(\beta)\), let \(q_T\) be the exact lower-tail cutoff, and let \(a_T\) include the common boundary randomization.  Relative to \(P_{0,T}\), the exact design has density
\[
w_T(z)=\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}a_{T,H_T}(z),
\qquad E_{0,T}w_T=1,
\qquad \eta\leq w_T\leq \eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}.
\tag{3}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\), \(H_T\to G_\infty(\beta)\) uniformly.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}oracle\text{-}rank}\), the limiting quadratic form has positive rank, so its Gaussian distribution has no atom at its positive \(\alpha\)-quantile.  Equation (1), quantile convergence, and the portmanteau theorem now give, for every bounded continuous \(h\),
\[
E_{0,T}\{h(X_{T,\beta},Z_T)a_{T,H_T}\}
\longrightarrow
E\left[h(U_\beta,Z)
\mathbf 1\{Z^{\mathsf T}G_\infty(\beta)Z\leq q_{\alpha,\beta}\}\right].
\tag{4}
\]
Any finite-sample mass placed at the cutoff tends to zero, so the randomized-tie term disappears in (4).  The exact lower-tail optimality at every finite \(T\), including atoms, is supplied by \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}lower\text{-}tail\text{-}identity}\).

It remains to check that exact Horvitz--Thompson inclusion weights do not alter the first-order limit.  Conditional on \(Z_i=q\), the remaining allocation is again a complete random partition with cell sizes differing from the unconditional ones by at most one and with one bounded observation removed.  The same negligible-influence calculation and the cited random-partition theorem give the same Gaussian quadratic limit, uniformly in \(i,q,\beta\).  Hence (3)--(4) imply
\[
\sup_{i\in T,q\in\mathcal Q,\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|\pi_{iq}(T,G_T(\beta))-Q^{-1}\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]
Writing the exactly centered estimator with summands
\[
\frac{\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}-\pi_{iq}}{\pi_{iq}}Y_{in}(q)
\]
and using (5) gives the same joint Gaussian limit under the tilted laws (3).  This centered representation is the reason that no rate stronger than the convergence in (5) is required at first order.

The mixture lower bound also gives \(\pi_{iq}\geq\eta/Q\).  Bounded outcomes, bounded inverse inclusion weights, and the fourth-moment identity for sampling without replacement yield
\[
\sup_{T,\beta}E\|X_{T,\beta}\|^4<\infty
\tag{6}
\]
for the full sequence and, in expectation over the split, for random complements with \(N\to\infty\).  Thus the quadratic losses are uniformly integrable.  Combining (3)--(6) gives, uniformly in \(\beta\),
\[
kV_T(0,\beta)\longrightarrow E(U_\beta^{\mathsf T}WU_\beta),
\]
and
\[
kV_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\longrightarrow
\eta E(U_\beta^{\mathsf T}WU_\beta)
+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}
E\left[U_\beta^{\mathsf T}WU_\beta
\mathbf 1\{Z^{\mathsf T}G_\infty(\beta)Z\leq q_{\alpha,\beta}\}\right].
\tag{7}
\]
Their difference is exactly \(a(\beta)\), proving the two asserted one-wave convergences; (6) and (2) give the stated \(L^1(P_{S_m})\) form for random complements.

For positivity, put \(R_\beta=\operatorname{Cov}(U_\beta,Z)\) and \(M_\beta=R_\beta^{\mathsf T}WR_\beta\).  Gaussian projection gives
\[
E(U_\beta\mid Z)=R_\beta Z,
\]
and the residual covariance cancels between the two terms in (7), because the acceptance event has probability \(\alpha\).  Since
\(G_\infty(\beta)=M_\beta/\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)\),
\[
a(\beta)
=(1-\eta)\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)
\left[
E g_\beta(Z)-\alpha^{-1}E\{g_\beta(Z)
\mathbf 1(g_\beta(Z)\leq q_{\alpha,\beta})\}
\right],
\quad g_\beta(z)=z^{\mathsf T}G_\infty(\beta)z.
\tag{8}
\]
The bracket is strictly positive: by the finite lower-tail identity the lower \(\alpha\)-tail has no larger mean than acceptance independent of \(g_\beta\), and strictness follows because \(0<\alpha<1\), the Gaussian density is positive, and \(g_\beta(Z)\) is nonconstant by the positive-rank condition.  The raw-oracle signal floor and convergence of the raw projection matrices give
\[
\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{tr}(M_\beta)>0.
\tag{9}
\]
The upper bound is finite by bounded second moments.  Continuity of the covariance blocks, \(G_\infty\), and \(q_{\alpha,\beta}\), together with dominated convergence and the zero-boundary-mass property, makes (8) continuous in \(\beta\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal K\), (8), and (9) prove the asserted uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds.

Finally set
\[
D_{n,m}(\beta)=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta).
\]
Since \(m/n\to c\) and \(N/n\to1-c\), the two one-wave limits give
\[
nD_{n,m}(\beta)
=nd_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\frac Nn E_{S_m}\{N d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\}
\longrightarrow a(\beta)-(1-c)a(\beta)=c a(\beta)
\]
uniformly in \(\beta\).  This algebra uses only first-order convergence and therefore yields no coefficient for the smaller \(m/n^2\) contrast when \(c=0\).

The pilot split and its balanced complete randomization are parameter-free.  The baseline law is the point mass at \(\mathbf X_n\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}baseline}\), and conditional outcomes are independent by \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\).  Consequently the factors for \(S_m\), \(Z_{S_m}\), and \(\mathbf X_n\) cancel from the likelihood ratio, while unobserved potential outcomes integrate to one.  What remains is
\[
\frac{dP_{\beta+v/\sqrt m}^{\mathcal O_m}}
{dP_{\beta}^{\mathcal O_m}}
=\prod_{i\in S_m}
\frac{p_{Z_i,\beta+v/\sqrt m}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in})}
{p_{Z_i,\beta}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in})},
\]
and taking logarithms proves the first display.  Quadratic-mean differentiability identifies the conditional score central sequence as
\[
\Delta_m(\beta)=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in S_m}
s_{Z_i,\beta}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in}).
\]
Each summand has conditional mean zero, and the product law makes distinct summands conditionally independent.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\beta\{\Delta_m(\beta)\mid S_m,Z_{S_m},\mathbf X_n\}
=\frac1m\sum_{i\in S_m}
E_\beta(s_{Z_i,\beta}s_{Z_i,\beta}^{\mathsf T}\mid x_{in})
=\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m}),
\]
which proves the information identity.

We now give an explicit certificate that convergence to \(I(\beta)\) is not implied.  Take \(p=1\), let \(\nu\) be Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]\), and choose an equidistributed triangular array consisting entirely of rational points.  It is bounded, converges weakly to \(\nu\), and can be chosen with empirical variance bounded away from zero.  Define the bounded measurable function
\[
h(x)=1+\mathbf 1\{x\in\mathbb Q\}.
\]
Choose distinct bounded support points \(y_1,\ldots,y_J\), strictly positive probabilities \(p_1^0,\ldots,p_J^0\), and a nonzero vector \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_J)\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{j=1}^Jv_j=\sum_{j=1}^Jy_jv_j
=\sum_{j=1}^Jy_j^2v_j=0.
\tag{10}
\]
For example, for \((-2,-1,0,1,2)\) one may take \(v=(1,-4,6,-4,1)\).  For \(|\theta|\) in a sufficiently small compact interval, set
\[
p_{q,\theta}(y_j\mid x)=p_j^0+\theta h(x)v_j
\qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
\tag{11}
\]
Positivity follows by shrinking the interval.  Equation (10) makes the first two conditional moments in (11) constant in \((x,\theta)\), so all stated moment-smoothness conditions hold.  Finite support and uniform positivity give uniform quadratic-mean differentiability and bounded third score moments.  At \(\theta=0\), however,
\[
E_0\{s_{q,0}^2\mid x\}
=h(x)^2\sum_{j=1}^J\frac{v_j^2}{p_j^0}.
\tag{12}
\]
Because every array point is rational, the empirical average of (12) equals four times the constant on the right without \(h(x)^2\), whereas its \(\nu\)-integral equals that constant because the rationals have Lebesgue measure zero.  Balanced assignment and uniform sampling of the pilot do not remove this discrepancy: the corresponding entry of \(\mathcal I_m\) converges in probability to four times the corresponding entry of \(I(0)\).

The construction can be embedded in the full regular chart by taking further linearly independent finite-support perturbation directions.  The direction (10) may be assigned to a nuisance coordinate, so it changes neither the first two moments nor \(G_T\); a regular oracle-coordinate block can therefore retain the oracle-smoothness, rank, signal, and curvature conditions.  If necessary, the same zero-moment perturbation may instead be added to a regular oracle score direction without changing its moment derivatives.  Thus the missing score-information convergence is not a consequence of the remaining model conditions.  Without that convergence, quadratic-mean differentiability does not identify the experiment with the Gaussian shift having information \(I(\beta)\), and neither nuisance-efficient covariance \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-1}\) nor a decision-theoretic action bound with constant \(B(\beta)\) follows.  The additional exact finite-boundary transfer is separately posed in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}finite\text{-}boundary\text{-}comparison}\).

For any pilot-measurable action \(\delta_m\), expand the last two terms of the exact accounting identity using
\(d_T(\beta)=V_T(0,\beta)-V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\).  The oracle main-wave terms cancel exactly and give
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)
-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(0,\beta)\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Risk is nonnegative, so the first main-wave term inside braces is at least zero.  For the fixed member, arraywise moment regularity supplies a finite common conditional second-moment envelope.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}single\text{-}wave\text{-}risk}\) with \(H=0\) therefore gives a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), the split, and \(\beta\), such that
\[
V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(0,\beta)\leq \frac C N.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (15)--(16), at the fixed \(\beta_0\), imply for every \(\delta_m\)
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
\geq d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)-\frac{CN}{n^2}.
\tag{17}
\]
The first-order oracle-gain theorem gives
\[
n d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\longrightarrow a(\beta_0)>0.
\tag{18}
\]
Because \(N/n\to0\), (17)--(18) yield, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
\geq \frac{a(\beta_0)}{2n}>0
\]
uniformly over \(\delta_m\).  Hence, using the definition of \(\mathcal E_n\),
\[
\mathcal E_n(m)
=\inf_{\delta_m}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)]_+
\geq \frac{a(\beta_0)}{2n}.
\]
Multiplication by \(n^{3/2}\) gives the claimed divergence.

By \(\mathrm{lem{:}deterministic\text{-}envelope\text{-}certificate}\), \(\Phi\) has the unique minimizer \(t^{\star}>0\), its minimum is \(C^{\star}>0\), and the convex-hull formula and two-active-point certificate in the statement hold.  It remains to transfer this deterministic conclusion to the balanced discrete problems.

Because \(Q\mid n\), every multiple of \(Q\) has a balanced complement.  Choose \(\widetilde m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) to be a nearest admissible multiple of \(Q\) to \(t^{\star}\sqrt n\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), this point is between \(Q\) and \(n-Q\), and
\[
\left|\frac{\widetilde m_n}{\sqrt n}-t^{\star}\right|
\leq\frac Q{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
Choose \(0<a<t^{\star}<b<\infty\).  Premise \((\mathrm I)\), continuity of \(\Phi\), and (19) give
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\widetilde m_n)\longrightarrow
\Phi(t^{\star})=C^{\star}.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus, with \(e_n=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) (the minimum exists because \(\mathcal M_n\) is finite),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}e_n\leq C^{\star}.
\tag{21}
\]

Let \(\ell_n\) be an exact minimizer.  By (20), \(n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell_n)\leq C^{\star}+1\) eventually.  Premise \((\mathrm{II})\) forces the ratios \(\ell_n/\sqrt n\) to remain bounded away from both zero and infinity.  Indeed, failure of either bound would produce a subsequence converging to the corresponding endpoint and contradict \((\mathrm{II})\).  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence on which
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t_0\in(0,\infty).
\]
On a compact interval containing that subsequence, premise \((\mathrm I)\) yields
\[
n^{3/2}e_n-\Phi(\ell_n/\sqrt n)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{22}
\]
Equations (21)--(22) imply \(\Phi(t_0)\leq C^{\star}\).  Minimality of \(C^{\star}\) gives equality, and uniqueness gives \(t_0=t^{\star}\).  Since every convergent subsequence has this limit,
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t^{\star},
\qquad n^{3/2}e_n\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\tag{23}
\]
Because \(C^{\star}>0\), (23) also proves \(e_n>0\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Now let \(m_n\) satisfy \(\mathcal E_n(m_n)/e_n\to1\).  From (23),
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)
=\frac{\mathcal E_n(m_n)}{e_n}\,n^{3/2}e_n
\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\tag{24}
\]
Premise \((\mathrm{II})\) again confines \(m_n/\sqrt n\) to a compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\).  Along any convergent subsequence with limit \(t_1\), premise \((\mathrm I)\) and (24) give \(\Phi(t_1)=C^{\star}\).  Uniqueness forces \(t_1=t^{\star}\), proving convergence of the full sequence and completing the implication.

added_lemmas.statement: Let a deterministic finite population of uniformly bounded vector attributes be partitioned by complete randomization into a fixed number \(Q\) of groups whose limiting proportions are strictly positive.  If the finite-population covariance matrices converge and the largest squared centered attribute is negligible relative to the total quadratic variation in every nondegenerate projection, then every fixed linear contrast of the group means converges, after normalization by its randomization covariance, to a centered Gaussian law.  The multivariate conclusion follows by the Cram\'{e}r--Wold device.

For every member of \(\mathfrak M\), every \(m\in\mathcal M_n\), every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), and every pilot-measurable normalized centered action \(\delta_m\),
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
=D_{n,m}(\beta)+L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta).
\]
Thus there is no third cross-wave term.  If
\(s_{n,m}=m/n^2+1/(nm)\), then the desired uniform coefficient expansion is equivalent to
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\frac{\left|D_{n,m}(\beta)-A(\beta)m/n^2
+L_{n,m}(\widehat G_m,\beta)-B(\beta)/(nm)\right|}{s_{n,m}}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular, whenever either one of the two component remainders is \(o(s_{n,m})\) uniformly, the total expansion holds if and only if the other component remainder is \(o(s_{n,m})\) uniformly.  After subtracting the action-independent term \(D_{n,m}\), every arbitrary-action lower bound for the total excess risk is exactly the corresponding lower bound for \(L_{n,m}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The exact accounting theorem gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
&=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\\
&\quad+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\!\left[
V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)
-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}
\{G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The first line on the right of (13) is \(D_{n,m}(\beta)\), and the second is \(L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)\), by \(\mathrm{def{:}risk\text{-}components}\).  This proves the identity and shows directly that no additional covariance or cross-wave term remains after exact Horvitz--Thompson centering.

Put
\[
s_{n,m}=\frac m{n^2}+\frac1{nm},\qquad
e_D(\beta)=D_{n,m}(\beta)-A(\beta)\frac m{n^2},
\]
and
\[
e_L(\delta_m,\beta)=L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-\frac{B(\beta)}{nm}.
\]
Subtracting the two proposed coefficients from (13) gives the exact residual identity
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
-A(\beta)\frac m{n^2}-\frac{B(\beta)}{nm}
=e_D(\beta)+e_L(\delta_m,\beta).
\tag{14}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\beta\) and dividing by \(s_{n,m}\) proves the displayed equivalence.  If \(\sup_\beta|e_D(\beta)|/s_{n,m}\to0\), the triangle inequality applied to (14), in both directions, shows that the total residual is uniformly \(o(s_{n,m})\) if and only if \(e_L(\widehat G_m,\cdot)\) is.  The symmetric assertion follows when \(e_L\) is already controlled.  Finally, for every action and every deterministic benchmark \(b_{n,m}(\beta)\), (13) gives
\[
\{R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)-D_{n,m}(\beta)\}
-b_{n,m}(\beta)
=L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-b_{n,m}(\beta).
\]
All pointwise suprema, local suprema, and infima over pilot-measurable actions are therefore identical on the two sides.  This proves the lower-bound reduction without asserting either unresolved coefficient estimate.
added_lemmas.justification: This exact reduction isolates the two and only two quantities that a future second-order comparison must control.
added_lemmas.gap: Horvitz--Thompson centering and Yamin's pooled-risk accounting motivate the decomposition but do not supply either factorial coefficient.
added_lemmas.consumer: It gives the finite-boundary analysis a precise pair of separately auditable targets.

added_lemmas.statement: Can one add no new model assumption but nevertheless obtain an existing subsequential limit of \(\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m})\), establish triangular-array LAN relative to that limit, localize arbitrary measurable normalized actions, and transfer the Gaussian quadratic loss with curvature \(\Gamma(\beta)\) to the exact Horvitz--Thompson action regret?  The handle is a subsequence audit of the empirical score-information measures followed by a conditional Gaussian-shift decision argument and the finite-boundary comparison.
added_lemmas.justification: This question separates the missing information limit from the missing exact-action comparison.
added_lemmas.gap: Armstrong's LAN efficiency results require an information limit and do not provide the exact Horvitz--Thompson boundary transfer.
added_lemmas.consumer: Resolving it would determine whether the candidate trace constant is an attainable and minimax action-regret coefficient.

added_lemmas.statement: Can a finite-pilot two-point testing argument give a strictly positive minimax excess-risk floor when \(m\) remains bounded?  The handle is to choose two interior parameter values with separated oracle actions but mutually contiguous finite pilot laws and to lower-bound the action regret under at least one value.
added_lemmas.justification: A bounded pilot must be excluded by finite-information testing rather than an interior asymptotic expansion.
added_lemmas.gap: No current core result supplies a two-point action-separation lower bound for finitely many pilot outcomes.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is one of the endpoint inputs needed by the conditional argmin transfer.

added_lemmas.statement: Can a local-action lower bound show \(n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\to\infty\) when \(m\to\infty\) but \(m=o(\sqrt n)\)?  The handle is the LAN-to-action bridge with the empirical information limit and exact finite-boundary localization made explicit.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the vanishing-pilot endpoint of the proposed square-root balance.
added_lemmas.gap: Its expected divergence is only heuristic until the LAN and exact finite-action bridges are proved.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the lower-end coercivity premise in the conditional global theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Can the sharp deletion expansion show \(n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\to\infty\) when \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\)?  The handle is an order-two one-wave expansion uniform over exact ties and unequal inclusion probabilities, followed by random-complement moment cancellation.
added_lemmas.justification: First-order equivalence is too coarse to exclude pilots larger than the candidate square-root scale but still negligible relative to the experiment.
added_lemmas.gap: The required positive order-two deletion coefficient is not supplied by the available finite-population central limit theorems.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the upper-interior coercivity premise in the conditional global theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Can a first-order arbitrary-action Gaussian oracle comparison exclude positive pilot fractions satisfying \(m/n\to c\in(0,1)\) and \(N\asymp n\)?  The handle is to combine the positive macroscopic deletion coefficient \(c a(\beta)\) with a uniform first-order lower comparison showing that a learned finite action cannot offset the oracle deletion loss.
added_lemmas.justification: The positive first-order deletion cost must be compared against every possible learned main-wave action.
added_lemmas.gap: The current core has no arbitrary-action Gaussian oracle comparison on a positive pilot-fraction window.
added_lemmas.consumer: It rules out macroscopic pilots in the endpoint-coercivity premise.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every member of \(\mathfrak M\), let \(a(\beta)\) be the first-order Gaussian exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient defined in the symbol table.  It is continuous on \(\mathcal K\) and satisfies
\[
0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}a(\beta)
\leq \sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}a(\beta)<\infty .
\]
Along the full-array sequence,
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|n d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-a(\beta)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every balanced sequence with \(N\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to c\in[0,1)\), the random complement obeys
\[
E_{S_m}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|N d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)-a(\beta)\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
and consequently
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|n\left\{d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\right\}
-c a(\beta)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This first-order conclusion does not assert the sharper pilot-frontier expansion of order \(m/n^2\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Available random-partition limits identify the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain but give no rate strong enough for the original pilot-frontier deletion coefficient.
The current assumptions yield exact outcome-only likelihood factorization but do not force convergence of the empirical score information or the exact finite-action loss comparison.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix a member of \(\mathfrak M\) and a parameter value \(\beta_0\in\mathcal K\).  For every balanced pilot-size sequence \(m\in\mathcal M_n\) with \(N=n-m=o(n)\),
\[
\mathcal E_n(m)\geq \frac{a(\beta_0)}{2n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Consequently
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
No endpoint conclusion is asserted here for bounded \(m\), for \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), for \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), or for positive pilot fractions with \(N\asymp n\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Exact accounting and first-order oracle gain prove only the nearly-all-pilot endpoint; the other four windows require distinct lower bounds not present in the core.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume the following two statistical premises.  First, for every \(0<a<b<\infty\),
\[
\sup_{\substack{\ell\in\mathcal M_n\\a\leq \ell/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell)-\Phi(\ell/\sqrt n)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{I}
\]
Second, sequential endpoint coercivity holds: for every sequence \(\ell_n\in\mathcal M_n\),
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow\infty
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell_n)\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{II}
\]
Then \(e_n=\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(n\), and every \(m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfying \(\mathcal E_n(m_n)/e_n\to1\) obeys
\[
\frac{m_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t^{\star},
\qquad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
C^{\star}=\min_{t>0}\Phi(t)
=\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}
2\sqrt{ab}>0,
\]
the minimizer \(t^{\star}\) is unique, and an optimizing convex combination is supported on at most two parameter values active at \(t^{\star}\).  This is a conditional argmin-transfer theorem; it does not assert premises \((\mathrm I)\) and \((\mathrm{II})\) from the current statistical assumptions.

proposed.statement:
For every member of \(\mathfrak M\), let \(a(\beta)\) be the first-order Gaussian exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient defined in the symbol table.  It is continuous on \(\mathcal K\) and satisfies
\[
0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}a(\beta)
\leq \sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}a(\beta)<\infty .
\]
Along the full-array sequence,
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|n d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-a(\beta)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every balanced sequence with \(N\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to c\in[0,1)\), the random complement obeys
\[
E_{S_m}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|N d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)-a(\beta)\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
and consequently
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left|n\left\{d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\right\}
-c a(\beta)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This first-order conclusion does not assert the sharper pilot-frontier expansion of order \(m/n^2\).

proposed.statement:
Assume the following two statistical premises.  First, for every \(0<a<b<\infty\),
\[
\sup_{\substack{\ell\in\mathcal M_n\\a\leq \ell/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell)-\Phi(\ell/\sqrt n)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{I}
\]
Second, sequential endpoint coercivity holds: for every sequence \(\ell_n\in\mathcal M_n\),
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow\infty
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell_n)\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{II}
\]
Then \(e_n=\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(n\), and every \(m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfying \(\mathcal E_n(m_n)/e_n\to1\) obeys
\[
\frac{m_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t^{\star},
\qquad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
C^{\star}=\min_{t>0}\Phi(t)
=\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}
2\sqrt{ab}>0,
\]
the minimizer \(t^{\star}\) is unique, and an optimizing convex combination is supported on at most two parameter values active at \(t^{\star}\).  This is a conditional argmin-transfer theorem; it does not assert premises \((\mathrm I)\) and \((\mathrm{II})\) from the current statistical assumptions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A subsequential empirical score-information limit, triangular-array LAN, arbitrary-action localization, and exact Horvitz--Thompson curvature transfer.
open_obligations.obstruction: Weak convergence of baseline empirical measures controls bounded continuous functions, but the current assumptions impose no baseline continuity on conditional score second moments; the exact finite-boundary comparison is also unresolved.
open_obligations.attempted: Factored the pilot likelihood and computed its conditional information. A rational-grid finite-support family shows directly that the random empirical information can converge to a matrix different from the defined population information.
open_obligations.partial_result: The exact likelihood factorization and conditional information identity are proved.  An explicit rational-grid finite-support family shows that \(\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m})\) need not converge to \(I(\beta)\); a LAN-to-action conclusion therefore requires a subsequential information analysis and the still-open finite-boundary bridge.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A finite-pilot two-point testing lower bound for separated oracle actions.
open_obligations.obstruction: A bounded number of pilot outcomes lies outside LAN, and the current core contains neither a finite-experiment testing affinity bound nor a uniform action-separation lemma.
open_obligations.attempted: Used exact risk accounting to isolate action regret, but no available result lower-bounds it from finitely many pilot observations.
open_obligations.partial_result: Exact Horvitz--Thompson accounting reduces the problem to lower-bounding the action regret from a pilot experiment with bounded information.  No frozen result supplies the required two-point separation and testing bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The local-action lower bound when the pilot diverges more slowly than \(\sqrt n\).

open_obligations.attempted: Computed the candidate Gaussian quadratic constant and isolated the missing empirical-information convergence with an explicit counterexample.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A positive sharp deletion term for \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: A first-order Gaussian oracle lower comparison uniform over all pilot-measurable main-wave actions when the pilot fraction is positive.

prose_updates.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal mixture yield an exactly unbiased pooled Horvitz--Thompson estimator for the realized factorial vector. The verified asymptotic result is first-order: the full-array and random-complement oracle gains converge after multiplication by wave size to a continuous uniformly positive Gaussian mixture coefficient \(a(\beta)\), giving macroscopic deletion loss \(c a(\beta)/n\) when \(m/n\to c\). Exact accounting decomposes every excess risk into the deletion term \(D_{n,m}\) and learned-action term \(L_{n,m}\), with no third cross-wave term. The pilot likelihood factors exactly through observed outcomes, but the present assumptions do not force its empirical score information to converge to \(I(\beta)\). The square-root pilot constant is therefore established only by a conditional argmin-transfer theorem; its statistical compact-window expansion and remaining endpoint bounds are open finite-boundary and information-limit problems.

project_justification.gap: The closest factorial sample-splitting procedure establishes first-order oracle equivalence but leaves refined learning-sample choice open. Existing binary-arm pilot theory, LAN efficiency theory, and finite-population Gaussian approximation do not supply the score-weighted moving-boundary expansion with exact ties and unequal Horvitz--Thompson inclusions required here.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic complete baseline array and a locally rich bounded outcome chart make it possible to separate three issues cleanly: first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, pilot score-information convergence, and the genuinely second-order finite-boundary comparison.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact Horvitz--Thompson accounting, a continuous uniformly positive first-order oracle-gain coefficient, an exact pilot likelihood and information audit, the nearly-all-pilot endpoint, and a conditional global argmin transfer. It reduces the proposed second-order frontier to explicit deletion and action-regret comparisons and records the unresolved information and endpoint obligations without claiming their coefficients.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on the parameter-free pilot split and assignment, the likelihood is the product of the observed outcome densities and has random empirical information \(\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m})\). The current arraywise moment assumptions do not imply convergence of this matrix to \(I(\beta)\), so nuisance-efficient estimation and the trace action-regret constant remain conditional targets rather than established properties.

prose_updates.related_work: Li and Ding's random-partition central limit theorems support the first-order joint Gaussian limit used for the exact-mixture oracle gain; they do not provide the order-two moving-boundary rate. Han and Deng supply the closest data-adaptive factorial architecture and first-order oracle equivalence, while explicitly leaving refined learning-sample choice beyond their result. Yamin's pooled binary-arm analysis motivates the deletion-versus-action decomposition and conditional argmin architecture, but its \(n^{2/3}\) rate comes from a different regret boundary and is not transplanted here. Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds apply after an average-information limit is established; the present likelihood audit shows that such convergence is not implied by the current deterministic-array assumptions. Wang and Li's convex-set Gaussian bounds do not control the score-weighted exact-alpha boundary moments at the required order. Horvitz and Thompson justify inverse-inclusion centering, while the exact pooled identity here accommodates randomized ties and unequal inclusions. Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate the stable-batch factorial-cycle consumer, but no preregistered square-root pilot rule is claimed until the open statistical premises are proved.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite exact-alpha action can change discontinuously when a score coordinate crosses a lattice tie, and exact inclusion probabilities can be unequal. First-order weak convergence absorbs boundary atoms because the limiting Gaussian quadratic form has zero boundary mass, but it supplies no remainder at order \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\). Independently, smooth first two outcome moments do not control conditional score information as a function of the baseline: the rational-grid finite-support witness in the likelihood audit makes the empirical pilot information differ from \(I(\beta)\). These are separate obstructions and neither is assumed away.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness and risk accounting, the memberwise one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the continuous uniformly positive first-order exact-mixture gain \(a(\beta)\), exact likelihood factorization with an information-limit counterexample, the exact \(D_{n,m}+L_{n,m}\) reduction, the nearly-all-pilot endpoint, and the deterministic conditional argmin transfer. The coefficient \(A(\beta)\), the transfer of \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) to exact finite action regret, the remaining endpoint windows, and the unconditional square-root pilot frontier remain open. The causal estimand continues to be the realized finite-population factorial vector under the stated randomization; the conditional outcome family averages design risk and does not redefine that estimand.
